sentences.text: Corynebacterium propinquum is a Gram-positive species that frequently colonises the upper respiratory tract and has been reported to associate strongly with a reduced incidence of respiratory tract infections.

Among 183 Corynebacterium strains isolated from patients undergoing preoperative examinations for cataract surgery, Corynebacterium accolens and Corynebacterium propinquum were the two major species of the nasal cavity, at 44% and 31%.

In synthetic nasal communities, consortia dominated by specific Corynebacterium propinquum strains excluded most other members including Staphylococcus aureus, and the species outcompeted S. aureus in nasal-like conditions.

In nasopharyngeal samples from 96 young children, the genus Corynebacterium showed a consistent inverse relationship with Streptococcus pneumoniae colonisation, and isolated Corynebacterium propinquum inhibited growth of a pneumococcal strain in vitro.

In mice, nasal priming with Corynebacterium propinquum or Corynebacterium pseudodiphtheriticum was associated with a modulated inflammatory response and a reduced pneumococcal burden in the respiratory tract.
